candidates.statement: Use Uber mainly to get transportation from one place to another.

evidence_candidates.quote: For me, the main goal is transportation to get from one place to another.

candidates.statement: Decide whether to take a ride by weighing how long the trip takes and what it costs.
context: Only when unable or unwilling to drive, or when no better transport option exists

evidence_candidates.quote: When I've chosen to look for a ride, it's usually the amount of time it will take or the price in deciding whether or not to take ride.
It's usually like whether or not I'm able to drive there or I want to drive there or if there are other better means of transportation, which kind of depends on again the price and duration.

candidates.statement: Walk instead of taking a ride when the ride would take about an hour and a half.
context: Even if the destination is far away

evidence_candidates.quote: So if it's going to take like an hour and a half to get someplace. So I'll just walk even if it's kind of far away.

candidates.statement: Choose the cheapest ride option, except when traveling with more people.

evidence_candidates.quote: I usually just go for The cheapest one, to be honest, unless if i'm going with more people

candidates.statement: See nearby drivers on a map to know whether drivers are available near me.

evidence_candidates.quote: I can also see a map with a couple different Ubers around. So I can know if there are other drivers near me.

candidates.statement: Wait before booking when the price is too high.

evidence_candidates.quote: if the price was too high, then I can choose to wait

candidates.statement: Book a driver shown as nearby without a long scheduling wait or a 'can't find a driver' ending.

evidence_candidates.quote: sometimes when I click okay and try to book that driver, it will take a really long time to actually schedule it. And sometimes it will end up saying that can't find a driver.

candidates.statement: Avoid canceling rides in order to protect my passenger rating.

evidence_candidates.quote: I usually try not to cancel a ride because I think that that damages my like the drivers will see a rating of the passenger as well.

candidates.statement: Rent a car for work travel or vacations when walkability, driving needs and duration make it worthwhile.
context: Preferred over rideshare when traveling for work or on vacation

evidence_candidates.quote: Most of the time when I book or when I'm traveling for work or just traveling in general, I would probably prefer to rent a car.

But for the most part, I would choose to rent a car depending on the duration. So if I'm going on vacation for a week. And I know I'm going to need to be traveling a decent amount, then it would make more sense and give me a little bit more freedom to rent a car than to do a ride share every time I want to go someplace.

candidates.statement: Care less about price and more about time on work rideshare trips, because the employer covers the cost.

evidence_candidates.quote: on the times where I have needed to to use a rideshare for work i usually care less about the price and more about the time in that case because my work is going to cover it.

candidates.statement: Take the bus for planned routes, including work trips covered by a free bus pass.

evidence_candidates.quote: So I usually do take a bus for my like planned route. So for work, it's fairly simple. My work gives me a free bus pass, basically.

candidates.statement: Avoid taking a bus in an area I am not familiar with.

evidence_candidates.quote: Because I don't want to take a bus in a place I'm not familiar with

candidates.statement: Take Uber instead of the bus when the bus trip would be long, require walking, or involve multiple transfers.

evidence_candidates.quote: there are a lot of there are a lot of places where either it would take a really long time to take the bus or it just um you have to like end up walking someplace or take a couple different Like. other buses. And so if it's complicated like that, I would probably prefer And Uber in that case.

candidates.statement: Avoid using Uber Eats after a bad customer-service experience.

evidence_candidates.quote: I have used it. That is something that I have had bad experiences with, so I've stopped using it.
It was a mixture of a bad estimate poorly estimating the amount of time And then the customer service dealing with that was extraordinarily poor.

candidates.statement: Reach a human customer-support agent when I need an issue resolved.

evidence_candidates.quote: I found it very difficult because I wanted to talk to a person
if you actually want to actually resolve an issue, you're probably going to need more than what they're like

candidates.statement: Prefer a single destination over a multi-stop trip when using Uber.

evidence_candidates.quote: Most of the time, if I'm going to use Uber, I would prefer to just go to one location versus going to multiple ones.

candidates.statement: Keep multi-stop trips as quick as possible, avoiding long in-between stops.

evidence_candidates.quote: I always feel weird if I'm going to do that where one of the in-between stops takes too much time So I try to to do anything like that. I try to make it as quick as possible

candidates.statement: Call or message the driver in the app when the pickup point is hard to find or the area is busy.
context: House numbers hard to see, poor GPS, no place to pull over, many people around

evidence_candidates.quote: I actually find that very helpful. Especially if I'm someplace that's like either a little weird. So maybe the house numbers are hard to see or or GPS just isn't great in that location.
So calling or calling usually calling on their way to pick me up is usually really helpful

candidates.statement: Let the driver know in the app when a multi-stop trip is taking longer than expected.

evidence_candidates.quote: in the circumstance where I'm doing a multi-stop letting the driver know if maybe I'm taking a little bit longer or just to give them a heads up about what's going on is also helpful

candidates.statement: Give the driver a heads-up directly instead of changing the pickup location in the app.
context: When the pickup point needs to change

evidence_candidates.quote: I think most of the time when I do want to change it, I give the driver a heads up instead of doing it on the app.

candidates.statement: Adjust the pickup location in the app easily even when it was set from the current location.

evidence_candidates.quote: But now I think it's only really easy if you're not using your location from the start
when you have it be your location This is hard to do without actually booking a ride.

candidates.statement: Check the ride fare after the trip to split the charge with friends or use it as a receipt for reimbursement.

evidence_candidates.quote: I will go back And look at how much the ride was so that I could split split up the charge. Or if I'm doing it for work, then I can use that as a receipt to get reimbursed.

candidates.statement: Book a ride for now rather than scheduling one for later.

evidence_candidates.quote: I can also book it uh for now or later, I usually just do now. I rarely book something in the future.

candidates.statement: Pick an address suggestion while typing instead of finishing the full address.

evidence_candidates.quote: a couple of different options pop up as I'm typing it, which is kind of helpful. So I can just click on whatever comes up before I necessarily finish typing it.

candidates.statement: Have a flash promo automatically applied to the fare.

evidence_candidates.quote: telling me that there's a flash promo deal. that I guess it automatically applied.

candidates.statement: Rate and tip the driver after the ride.

evidence_candidates.quote: they give you the option to rate the driver And you have the the option to tip the driver too

candidates.statement: Know whether a cancellation carries a charge.

evidence_candidates.quote: I also don't remember if you get a a potential charge for that.

candidates.statement: Cancel a ride without first starting the ride just to cancel it.

evidence_candidates.quote: I kind of wish that I don't want to just start a ride to cancel it.

candidates.statement: Not review the ride's location or duration after the trip.

evidence_candidates.quote: But I don't really... look back at it for the location or the duration usually.

candidates.statement: Get an accurate time estimate for Uber Eats orders.

evidence_candidates.quote: It was a mixture of a bad estimate poorly estimating the amount of time And then the customer service dealing with that was extraordinarily poor.
